reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the plan still needed revising in the last round (round 3 of 3). I read gh.rs: land_pr, wait_for_checks, classify_checks, GhClient::api and the Pages rerun code. The plan puts the retry in the right place, inside land_pr's check wait. The new host calls reuse the existing retry and error-log path, and HostOperation::ReadChecks is used the same way rerun_pages already uses it. The bound and the merge gate are stated, and the demonstrations mostly fail without the behavior. One design gap is major. classify_checks reports Red as soon as one check fails, even while others are still pending, so the first wait usually ends before the failed workflow run has completed. GitHub refuses rerun-failed-jobs on a run that has not completed, and Decision 4 then turns that into Red with no rerun, which defeats the unattended landing in a common case. The plan should wait, within the bound, for the failed runs to complete before asking for the rerun, and test that case. The other findings are minor clarifications. Findings: major: The first Red often comes while the failed workflow run is still in progress, so the rerun is refused or finds nothing to rerun and the landing never retries. (Plan approach and Decision 4 (first wait ends on Red, then rerun_failed); gh.rs:990-1009 classify_checks, gh.rs:1244-1257 wait_for_checks); minor: The expected read count in the [Red, Red, Pending, Red] demonstration is garbled. (Demonstrations, criterion 2, the [Red, Red, Pending, Red] case); minor: A fixed allowance of three looks is a weak staleness signal when run_attempt is already in the reply.
